packageRules.description: Modules the build patches in vendor/, through this repository's patches or sonic-mgmt-common's patches/apply.sh, and openconfig/gnoi, whose newer versions raise the patched fsnotify through openconfig/bootz. A bump has to refresh the patch, so it opens on its own, and only on dashboard approval. A security update still opens, on its own (see vulnerabilityAlerts above, which repeats this list), and the patched-module label keeps the preset from labeling it automerge.
prBodyNotes: The build patches this module in `vendor/`, through this repository's `patches/` or sonic-mgmt-common's `patches/apply.sh`. A patch that still applies may no longer be correct for the new version, so check each one against it. An `openconfig/gnoi` update raises the patched `fsnotify` through `openconfig/bootz`; refresh its patch. This update is never labeled `automerge`.

packageRules.description: Renovate merges the security updates the preset labels automerge itself, once every check on the head commit has passed, with the renovate-approve app's approval. The condition repeats the preset's automerge rule, and the two change together.

go.mod pins sonic-mgmt-common to a master commit, so Go and Renovate resolve it without a checkout beside this one; the build replaces it with that checkout. Moving the pin weekly keeps go.mod and go.sum close to sonic-mgmt-common's own requirements. The versions it brings in are already reviewed there, so it merges once every check passes. It waits until sonic-mgmt-common's head commit is 7 days old, the release age Semgrep's blocking renovate-missing-minimum-release-age rule requires, so the pin moves after a week with no commits there. The preset rebases only labeled security updates when they fall behind, so this rule does too, or a base branch that requires branches up to date would hold it forever.
